newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Minister wants CA sale cancelled.
newsitem.headline: Minister wants CA sale cancelled.

text.p: The Austrian government should annul last January's sale of Creditanstalt to rival Bank Austria if Germany's WestLB goes through with a first option on Bank Austria shares, a leading conservative minister said.

Economy Minister Hannes Farnleitner, a member of the People's Party, said the first refusal deal between majority owner AVZ and Westdeutsche Landesbank Girozentrale was "a breach of faith" by Chancellor Viktor Klima's Social Democrats.

Vienna City holding company AVZ, whose board includes Bank Austria chief Gerhard Randa and several Social Democrat politicians, agreed in 1995 to give WestLB first refusal on its 45.15 percent of Bank Austria voting stock.
News of the agreement, apparently at odds with Vienna city plans to privatise Bank Austria while maintaining a majority Austrian interest, only emerged over the weekend.
"Either WestLB gives up its right or the sale of Creditanstalt to Bank Austria must be reversed," Farnleitner told Austrian television during a trip to Spain.
People's Party leader Wolfgang Schuessel expressed outrage that his party had not been informed of the deal.
Last week, Vienna politicians agreed to sell the AVZ stake and a further four percent of voting stock, currently placed with holding company Wiener Holding, over the next six years.
The council argues it has a right to decide on the future of the shareholding because it guarantees all AVZ liabilities.
Bank Austria won the Austrian state's 70 percent voting stake in Creditanstalt in January, after six years of failed attempts to privatise the country's most conservative bank.
The People's Party only agreed to a takeover by Bank Austria after it received assurances that the nation's politicians would gradually withdraw from Bank Austria too.
